title: The Day of the Half-Lit Staircase
skyStory: First quarter moon, exactly half lit and half shadow, still parked in Capricorn like a careful driver checking its mirrors. It looks like a light switch somebody left in the middle position. Saturn approves of the balance. Mars wants to flip it all the way on. The wind off the water argues both sides and then leaves early.

reading: Half moon, halfway decisions. You will be standing on the middle step of something today, an email half written or a plan half drawn, and your instinct will be to leap to the top. The [[Knight of Wands]] suggests taking one stair at a time, loudly, like a tiger climbing a creaky porch.

Around 4:10 pm the light will hit something in your room at an angle you have never noticed. Stop and look. Half light is when the cabin shows its secrets: dust motes, a scratch in the floor with a story, a forgotten note under a lamp. Finish one half-thing before dark and the moon will consider you even.
joel.mission: Find one task you started last week and finish only the next single step, then stop on purpose and grin.
joel.omen: A staircase with exactly one light bulb out. Proceed anyway; you know the way better than you think.
joel.elementWhy: one firm step at a time

reading: The [[Six of Swords]] drifts by on a grey November tide, the little boat halfway across the water. That is exactly where today feels. The far shore is visible and the near one is getting smaller. Nothing to rush. Joel has an oar.

Today the Mountain is unusually good at noticing what is already done. Make a quiet list in your head while you wash a cup or walk to the car: three things you have finished this year that nobody gave you a medal for. Then give yourself the medal. The stacked diamonds on your left middle finger will flash when you get to number three, which is how the sky applauds.
nancy.mission: Say out loud, to anyone or to the kettle, one thing you finished this year that deserves a parade.
nancy.omen: A boat or a picture of one, pointed toward the right. The crossing is going better than it feels.

together.text: Each of you pick one thing to finish by Nov 9, when this year of readings closes. Tell each other what it is in six words or fewer. On the last day, report back like sailors home from sea.

game.intro: First quarter, half-lit staircase. Saturn has turned out half the studio lights and wants the shortest wrong answer.
game.question: What do you flip to turn on a light?
